correctness.rationale: Graph energy strictly convex on the affine trace space for all finite p>1; coordinate symmetry enforces radiality. Exact layer-edge multiplicity d*binomial(d-1,k) and equality in weighted Holder force each gradient to be the reciprocal (p-1)-power of the binomial weight. Maximal gradient is at the boundary edge, so dividing by the original two-point Lipschitz slope gives the exact displayed operator norm. Fixed p and moving p/d limits follow from binomial unimodality, elementary large-binomial estimates, and uniform entropy Stirling estimates; d=2 is excluded from strict statements. A separate program checked 52 rational full-graph vertex solutions, 128 edges, 1968 nonlinear Euler equations and 7152 nonlinear edges; this finite verification does not prove the infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The p-voltages variational problem is prior art in Bridle–Zhu (2013), and continuum dimension/exponent degeneracy is prior art in El Alaoui et al. (2016) and Flores–Calder–Lerman (2019). Known p=2 antipodal hypercube resistance is expressly excluded from novelty. The new scope is a complete exact p-dependent Lipschitz extension-operator amplification formula for every dimension and finite p, plus a sharp moving-exponent entropy-integral profile in a deterministic Boolean cube. Direct cross-parameter/alias searches and claim-versus-implication comparisons revealed no covering full result, but residual bibliographic risk remains.
residual_risks: Classical two-terminal p-resistance reductions and antipodal Boolean-network calculations might contain the same evaluated p-dependent formula in less-indexed older literature.
The continuum dimension/exponent threshold is prior art; novelty is claimed only for the exact sharp discrete operator norm and entropy profile.
No independent external mathematical verification or exhaustive literature guarantee.

value.rationale: Sparse-label graph energy interpolation is a motivated regularity problem because the variational optimum can dramatically degrade endpoint Lipschitz stability despite existence of a norm-one extension. A complete all-parameter exact formula quantifies the degradation. The theorem identifies a sharp p/d scaling transition, complete divergent and constant regimes, and a nontrivial entropy-integral limiting profile not contained in generic variational existence theorems. This is more than one tiny finite count, without claiming a general downstream theorem.
